reason: Conversation 1 gives the expected path: confirm the element failure, isolate at the cooker switch and MCB, identify the part from the model and serial, check terminals and connectors for heat damage, and use an engineer only if wiring is scorched or the user is unsure. Conversation 2 repeats generic 'stop using, unplug' banners that don't fit a hard-wired cooker, and it never really answers the homeowner's questions about the part and DIY fitting. It also overstates the need for an engineer's test equipment and tells the user to keep the whole oven out of use, which is overcautious given the main oven works and nothing has tripped again. It does give sensible advice on the rating plate and on scorch checks, but it is less helpful and less proportionate.
